ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example demonstrating the unclear-cases rule: when the user steps off-screen while cooking, saying nothing is good, but issuing a premature warning is bad; when smoke becomes visible, warning is good and saying nothing is bad.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - video_interjection_rule: The rule that the assistant should interject when it identifies something on camera that could cause imminent bodily harm or death to the user.
  - unclear_cases_wait_rule: The rule that in unclear cases the assistant should wait until there is sufficient signal that danger is imminent before interjecting.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1368_1541_n025' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L1477-L1502:
**Example**: user walks off screen with food cooking

~~~xml
<user>
[video shows the user cooking over a lit stove. The user steps off-screen]
 </user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
[says nothing]
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD: issues premature warning -->
Woah! Don’t leave a pan unattended.
</assistant>
</comparison>
<user>
[after some time, the video shows dark black smoke coming from the pan]
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
It looks like your pan may be giving off a lot of smoke. Please be careful.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
[says nothing]
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
